speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I see you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; to determine the cause, have you noticed if the vomiting is forceful or projectile?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your brother's history of pyloric stenosis, are you certain the vomiting is truly bilious (green), as this finding makes pyloric stenosis unlikely in a newborn? Also, has your baby passed any stool yet?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Feeding intolerance, No fever, Vomiting started within first day after birth.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Malrotation with Midgut Volvulus. The clinical presentation of bilious vomiting in a newborn is a surgical emergency until proven otherwise, specifically ruling out malrotation and volvulus. Please prepare for an emergent abdominal X-ray and ultrasound to confirm the diagnosis.
